workingTitle: A gamma-ray burst reveals a patchy magnetic field
coreFacts: INTEGRAL/IBIS measured GRB 181201A as the fourth gamma-ray burst with a polarization detection in this instrument's sample.
The three highest-signal time bins give an integrated polarization degree of 81.5 +17.2/-15.7 percent.
The polarization angle changed modestly during the burst, while the photon spectrum evolved from hard to soft without violating the standard synchrotron limit.
The authors interpret the combination as compatible with synchrotron radiation from a locally coherent but globally patchy magnetic field in a non-axisymmetric jet.
A Compton-drag model viewed near the jet edge also remains viable, and the error bars do not allow the authors to choose strongly between the two.
caveats: Reliable time-resolved polarization values come from only three high-signal intervals; other intervals are unconstrained or lower limits.
Adjacent 10-second analysis windows overlap by 5 seconds and are therefore correlated.
Polarization and spectral analyses use different energy ranges, limiting a joint interpretation.
The authors plan an updated pipeline and state that absolute polarization values could change, although they expect the temporal trend to persist.
